author: Claude3
suite_result: 19/19 PASS on fixedPython3.12 -I -B in fresh inertfixtures

findings.problem: direct-launch bypasses the unchanged register and launch consumer checks promised byD031; common checks only rowset/capture count/freeze shape. It writes records for an invalid register key and null freeze policy/entry pins.
findings.reproduced: Both cases exit0 and create launchJSON; subsequent binding exits2 with L2_KEY or FREEZE_CODE_PINS.
findings.impact: Malformed root metadata is accepted at the prelaunch step and only refused when campaign import occurs, after the expensive direct batch could have launched. No invalid admission was demonstrated.
findings.required_fix: Validate all seven register entries and freeze code pins before direct-launch publication against unchanged pinned consumer contracts. Add MUST_FAIL tests asserting no output for malformed register and freeze pins. Any synthetic validation context must remain test/internal validation only and never become a root binding record.

notes.text: read_pin lacks O_NONBLOCK before its regular-file check, a running byte cap, and before/after fstat consistency. Metadata SHA still authenticates returned bytes, but malformed FIFO can block before refusal and a growing input bypasses the initial size cap. Recommend hardening and inert refusal tests.

The every-input-read-once claim is not true: MemSnapshot does not cache disk reads, so each of seven select_two_stage calls rereads the register; freeze and captures also get reread. Cache verified raw buffers and reuse them, or narrow the claim. No false admission demonstrated.

boundaries: Inert metadata and real runtime producer only; no scientific launch/run-tree/NGC reads; sources unmodified.
